```{r}
#Setting the working directory
setwd("/Users/joe/Desktop/Masters Program/Fall 2026/Fundamentals of Machine Learning/Module 6/Assignment 4")

#Reading in the csv to create the original data frame
Pharma <- read.csv("Pharmaceuticals.csv")
```

```{r}
#installing/loading all of the packages needed for the assignment

library(dplyr)
library(factoextra)
```

```{r}
#standardize the 9 numerical variables we will use for clustering

vars <- c("Market_Cap", "Beta", "PE_Ratio", "ROE", "ROA", "Asset_Turnover", "Leverage", "Rev_Growth", "Net_Profit_Margin")

StdPharma <- Pharma %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(vars), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
```
Things I know I need to do:

X standardize the numerical values in the dataset before clustering
    Done

_ determine the right weighting for different variables... How? IDK What some of these are...
    Coming back to this, I think I am over thinking it - Revenue growth, market cap & profit margin seem important based on research into what equity analysts would look at.
  
_ determine the right kind of distance measure to use e.g., euclidean, manhattan, etc.
```{r}
#Create table with only the 9 standardized variables for clustering
StdPharmaTrimmed <- StdPharma %>%
  select(Market_Cap, Beta, PE_Ratio, ROE, ROA, Asset_Turnover, Leverage, Rev_Growth, Net_Profit_Margin)
```

```{r}
#double checking whether there are many outliers int he data using the z score definition, just to make sure euclidean distance makes sense. I think manhattan would make sense were there a lot of outliers, but since there are few, I will stick with euclidean.
sapply(StdPharmaTrimmed, function(x) sum(abs(x) > 3, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
#Clustering with 4 centroids
set.seed(404)

#might as well start 100 times since small df
k4 <- kmeans(StdPharmaTrimmed, centers = 4, nstart = 100)
fviz_cluster(k4, data = StdPharmaTrimmed)

#Just taking an initial pass at clustering with no weights and 4 centroids

```

```{r}
#adding weights to variables that I'd anticipate and equities analyst might deem more important for investment decisions...
weights <- c(
  Market_Cap        = 1.5, #a clear way to differentiate size tier
  Rev_Growth        = 1.5, #clear growth signal
  Net_Profit_Margin = 1.5, #clear profit signal
  PE_Ratio          = 1.25, # valuation/expectations
  ROA               = 1,#keeping standard weight
  Leverage          = 1, #keeping standard
  Beta              = 0.75, # sector is defensive, so less discriminating on volitility
  ROE               = 0.75, # overlaps with ROA, margin, and leverage
  Asset_Turnover    = 1 # keep standard
)

# new dataframe with weights applied
StdPharmaWeighted <- sweep(StdPharmaTrimmed, 2, weights[names(StdPharmaTrimmed)], `*`)
```

```{r}
#Clustering with 4 centers on weighted data 
set.seed(404)

k4w <- kmeans(StdPharmaWeighted, centers = 4, nstart = 100)
fviz_cluster(k4w, data = StdPharmaWeighted)
```

```{r}
#cross tab to compare cluster assignments from equal weighting kmeans to the weighted kmeans.
table(equal = k4$cluster, weighted = k4w$cluster)
```

```{r}
#now going to start determining the right number of clusters for our data using the elbow method and the avg silhouette method. Also going to run this on weighted and unweighted data to see if I am changing the number of natural clusters in the data

set.seed(404)
#Visuals for un-weighted data
fviz_nbclust(StdPharmaTrimmed, kmeans, method = "wss")
fviz_nbclust(StdPharmaTrimmed, kmeans, method = "silhouette")
```

```{r}
#Visuals for weighted data

set.seed(404)
fviz_nbclust(StdPharmaWeighted, kmeans, method = "wss")
fviz_nbclust(StdPharmaWeighted, kmeans, method = "silhouette")

#Since I will run my clustering on the weighted data, I need to run the elbow and silhouette on this data. On the elbow chart, 4 seems to be the knee, describing that the benefit of increasing to 5 clusters is very little, and it doesn't do much to increase the similarity within clusters

#the silhouette seems to suggest that companies fit their clusters best with 3 or 5 clusters, but the trade off for 4 clusters is small...

#all in all, I am going with 4 clusters
```


```{r}
#final kmeans cluster, with decided number of 4, with weighting, and using euclidean distance...

set.seed(404)
k4_final <- kmeans(StdPharmaWeighted, centers = 4, nstart = 100)

k4_final$size #checking the size of the clusters to make sure there are no super small clusters... Looks good. Retlatively even size.

fviz_cluster(k4_final, data = StdPharmaWeighted)
```

```{r}
#attach final cluster assignments to standardized full table
StdPharma$cluster <-factor(k4_final$cluster)
```

```{r}
#look into avg z scores for each company to see what describes the cluster...
profile_z <- StdPharma %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(all_of(vars), mean), .groups = "drop")

profile_z %>% mutate(across(all_of(vars), ~ round(.x, 2)))

#Cluster 1 "Profit Challenged Small Caps"
#Cluster 2 "Large Profit Leaders"
#Cluster 3 "Mature Cash Cows"
#Cluster 4 "High Growth Small Caps"
```

```{r}
#Assigning cluster names in the dataframe

StdPharma <- StdPharma %>%
  mutate(cluster_name = recode(as.character(cluster),
    "1" = "Profit Challenged Small Caps",
    "2" = "Large Profit Leaders",
    "3" = "Mature Cash Cows",
    "4" = "High Growth Small Caps"
  ))
```
